description: Get a user's AniList anime or manga list. Returns a compact table of one row per entry by default (`format: "compact"`) — entry id, media id, MAL id, status, score, progress and title, which is what a sync, comparison or pick-something-to-watch task needs; switch to `format: "full"` only when you actually need dates, notes, custom lists, advanced scores or the status/custom-list grouping, since that response is roughly ten times larger per entry. Filter server-side with `statuses` rather than fetching everything and discarding — asking for just CURRENT costs a fraction of a whole-list read. Pass `sort` (e.g. UPDATED_TIME_DESC) to have AniList order the list before chunking, so a small `perChunk` returns the top entries by that key rather than an arbitrary slice. To answer "what did they finish/start in a period", use the `completedAt_*`/`startedAt_*` bounds (strict, server-side) instead of scanning the list — e.g. everything completed in 2026 is `completedAt_greater: {year: 2025, month: 12, day: 31}` plus `completedAt_lesser: {year: 2027}`; chunking then counts only the matching entries. Works for any public/unlisted user. Accepts an exact AniList username directly — no need to call search_user first unless you only have a partial/fuzzy name. Paginated by `chunk`/`perChunk` (AniList's own mechanism for this — counted across entries of ALL statuses combined, not per status), since a large list can otherwise return thousands of entries in one response; check `hasNextChunk` and increment `chunk` to keep paging. `perChunk` itself has no cap — AniList accepts values in the thousands, so raise it to pull a whole list in one call instead of paging through it. The collection AniList exposes here is capped at its ~11,000 most recently updated unique entries — irrelevant for virtually every account, but a hard ceiling if one is ever hit (older entries beyond it aren't retrievable through this field at all, by any chunk).

chunk.description: Chunk number for pagination (AniList paginates this list by chunk, not page).

completedAt_greater.description: Only entries completed strictly AFTER this date (AniList filters server-side; the bound date itself is excluded). An omitted month/day counts as 0, so {year: 2026} here means "from 2026-01-01 on". Entries with no date recorded never match.

year.description: Required — a date bound needs at least a year.

completedAt_lesser.description: Only entries completed strictly BEFORE this date (AniList filters server-side; the bound date itself is excluded). An omitted month/day counts as 0, so {year: 2026} here means "up to 2025-12-31". Entries with no date recorded also pass this bound on its own — pair it with the matching `_greater` bound to exclude them.

year.description: Required — a date bound needs at least a year.

format.description: How much of each entry to return. `compact` (default) is a tab-separated table of entry id, media id, MAL id, status, score (0-10), progress and title, one de-duplicated row per entry — enough for syncing, comparing or choosing, at about a tenth the size. `full` returns AniList's own grouped objects with dates, notes, repeat/priority, custom lists and advanced scores; use it only when you need one of those, or when you need to know which custom list an entry is filed under (`compact` drops the grouping — every row still carries its own status).

perChunk.description: Entries per chunk, counted across all statuses combined. Defaults to 25 so an unattended call stays small, but nothing caps it — pass a larger value (AniList accepts values in the thousands) to pull a whole list in one call instead of paging. A compact row is small (a few hundred fit easily); with `format: "full"` each entry carries its dates, notes, custom lists and advanced scores, so a few hundred entries is already a large response there.

sort.description: Order AniList applies server-side; later keys break ties in earlier ones (e.g. [SCORE_DESC, UPDATED_TIME_DESC]). Applied to the whole list BEFORE chunking — `chunk` 1 with `perChunk` 10 and UPDATED_TIME_DESC is the 10 most recently updated entries across all statuses — and again within each status/custom-list group. Groups are not interleaved, so `compact` rows (concatenated group by group) are ordered within each status, not globally; filter to one status with `statuses` for a single fully ordered run. Omit for AniList's default order (oldest-added first within each group).

startedAt_greater.description: Only entries started strictly AFTER this date (AniList filters server-side; the bound date itself is excluded). An omitted month/day counts as 0, so {year: 2026} here means "from 2026-01-01 on". Entries with no date recorded never match.

year.description: Required — a date bound needs at least a year.

startedAt_lesser.description: Only entries started strictly BEFORE this date (AniList filters server-side; the bound date itself is excluded). An omitted month/day counts as 0, so {year: 2026} here means "up to 2025-12-31". Entries with no date recorded also pass this bound on its own — pair it with the matching `_greater` bound to exclude them.

year.description: Required — a date bound needs at least a year.

statuses.description: Only return entries with these statuses (AniList filters server-side, so this genuinely shrinks the response — prefer it over fetching the whole list and discarding). Omit for every status. Custom-list groups are still returned in `full` when their entries match.

type.description: Whether to get the anime or manga list.

user.description: AniList user ID (as a number — a digit string is read as a username), or username.

name: get_user_list

columns.description: `compact` only: the tab-separated column names for `rows`, in order.

count.description: `compact` only: how many unique entries `rows` contains.

format.description: Which shape this response is in — echoes the `format` argument.

hasNextChunk.description: True if another `chunk` of this list is available.

advancedScores.description: Per-category advanced scores as AniList actually stores them, as a {category: score} map on the same 0-10 scale as `score` (so a value read here can be passed straight back to add_list_entry/update_list_entry's `advancedScores`). Every configured category is present — AniList stores 0 for any not set.

customLists.description: Every custom list configured on the account, with `enabled` showing whether THIS entry is filed under it. Naming a list here (via add_list_entry/update_list_entry) that isn't already in the account's `animeListOptions`/`mangaListOptions` `customLists` is silently a no-op on write — the list must exist first.

score.description: This user's own score for the entry, on a 0-10 scale (decimals allowed). It stays 0-10 on every account whatever the configured scoreFormat is, and matches the scale add_list_entry/update_list_entry take on write. This is NOT the 0-100 scale `averageScore`/`meanScore`/search_media's `averageScore_greater` filter use.

lists.description: `full` only: AniList's own status/custom-list groups, with full entries.

rows.description: `compact` only: one tab-separated row per entry, newline-separated, matching `columns`. An empty cell means AniList has no value for that field (e.g. no MAL id); a score of 0 means unscored.

title: Get a user's anime or manga list
